statement: In statistics, a residual is the difference between an observed value of an element of a statistical sample and the estimated value of the quantity of interest; for an observation $X_i$ in a univariate location model with sample mean $\overline{X}$, the residual is defined by $r_i = X_i - \overline{X}$, and in regression analysis, it is the deviation of an observed dependent variable from the fitted function.

symbols.meaning: residual of observation i (observable fitting deviation)
observed value of the i-th element of a statistical sample
sample mean of the observations, defined as \frac{X_1 + \cdots + X_n}{n}
statistical error (disturbance) of observation i relative to the population mean \mu
number of estimated model parameters in a regression (excluding intercept)

properties.property: The sum of the residuals within a random sample is necessarily zero: \sum_{i=1}^n r_i = 0
properties.why: follows directly from the definition of the sample mean

properties.property: The residuals within a sample are necessarily not independent
properties.why: their sum is constrained to be zero

properties.property: A residual is an observable estimate of the unobservable statistical error
properties.why: it is computed from observable sample data and estimators rather than unobservable population parameters

properties.property: For independent observations from a normal population N(\mu, \sigma^2), the sum of squared residuals divided by \sigma^2 follows a chi-squared distribution with n - 1 degrees of freedom: \frac{1}{\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n r_i^2 \sim \chi_{n-1}^2
properties.why: estimation of the unknown population mean by the sample mean consumes one degree of freedom

properties.property: The sum of squares of the residuals and the sample mean are independent of each other in normal samples
The mean residual is always zero for least-squares estimators
properties.why: least-squares estimation selects coefficients such that the sum of squared residuals is minimized

properties.property: In a linear regression with identically distributed errors, the variability of residuals is higher in the middle of the input domain than at the ends
properties.why: linear regressions fit endpoints better and endpoints exert greater influence on regression coefficients

assumptions.assumption: An observable sample of data points and a defined estimator of the quantity of interest (such as a sample mean or fitted regression function) exist
assumptions.breaks_when: The sample size is zero or the estimating function cannot be computed

assumptions.assumption: For the chi-squared distribution of normalized sum of squared residuals, the population is normally distributed with independent observations
assumptions.breaks_when: The underlying distribution is non-normal or observations are not chosen independently

assumptions.assumption: For linear regression residuals to be random about zero, the linear model specification correctly represents the data-generating process
assumptions.breaks_when: The true relationship is nonlinear (e.g., quadratic or higher-order polynomial)

failure_modes.signature: A scatterplot of residuals plotted against the independent variable exhibits a non-random pattern or trend
failure_modes.cause: The true function relating independent and dependent variables is nonlinear or higher-order polynomial rather than linear

failure_modes.signature: Residuals fan out with increasing or decreasing spread across the range of the independent variable
failure_modes.cause: The variance of the unobserved statistical errors is non-constant across data points

failure_modes.signature: Systematic underestimation of the unobserved error variance
failure_modes.cause: Dividing the sum of squared residuals by n rather than the residual degrees of freedom n - p - 1

failure_modes.mode: Spurious outlier detection from raw residuals
failure_modes.signature: Incorrectly identifying data points in the middle of the domain as outliers or failing to detect outliers at domain boundaries
failure_modes.cause: Comparing raw residuals without studentizing to adjust for non-constant residual variability across input values
